worksheet.title: Fix the Stack
worksheet.subtitle: Find the wrong block and fix it
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the block that points the wrong way and fix it.

parts.title: Programs can have bugs
parts.text: Sometimes a program has a bug: one block points the WRONG way, so Bit misses the star ★. A coder runs the program, finds the wrong block, and fixes it. Bit starts on box 1. The star is on box 4.

parts.title: Bit's program (it has a bug)
parts.note: Run it from the top and see — does Bit reach the star?

parts.title: Run it
parts.prompt: Run the program from box 1, one block at a time. Which box does Bit land on? Is it the star? Write the box number.

parts.title: Find the bug
parts.prompt: One block points the WRONG way and sends Bit back. Circle the block that should not be there (the ⬅).

parts.title: The fixed program
parts.note: Draw the right arrow in the empty block.

parts.title: You try — fix it
parts.prompt: Draw the arrow that fixes the bug so Bit reaches the star. Then run the fixed program — which box does Bit land on now?

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Finding and fixing a wrong block is called debugging. Run it, find the bug, fix it, run it again — until Bit reaches the star.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Kindergarten · Intro Block Coding
teacher_guide.title: Fix the Stack
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children debug a block program: they run it, see that Bit misses the star, find the one block that points the wrong way, and fix it so the program works. Run → find the bug → fix → run again is the debugging cycle, and it closes the Intro Block Coding unit.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children test a sequence, identify where it goes wrong, and correct it.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child writes a box number, circles a block, and draws one arrow.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet, a pencil, and a blue crayon. Optional: floor boxes 1-5 with a star on box 4 so children can walk the buggy program and feel Bit go the wrong way.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: run the buggy program together — ➡ to box 2, ⬅ back to box 1, ➡ to box 2. 'Bit is on box 2, not the star. Something is wrong.'
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — Bit lands on box 2 (not the star). Exercise 2 — the middle ⬅ block sent Bit backward; circle it.
3. YOU TRY: Exercise 3 — the fixed block should be ➡; the program becomes ➡ ➡ ➡ and Bit reaches box 4, the star.
4. Connect: 'Coders do this all the time — they run a program, find the wrong block, and fix it. That is debugging.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — the buggy program (➡ ⬅ ➡) from box 1 lands Bit on box 2. Not the star.
Ex 2 — the wrong block is the middle ⬅ (it sends Bit back one box).
Ex 3 — fix it to ➡: the program becomes ➡ ➡ ➡ and Bit lands on box 4, the star.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: children blame the first or last block — have them run step by step and watch exactly where Bit turns back.
Anchor: the wrong block is the one that moves Bit AWAY from the star.
Simplify: walk the buggy program on the floor so the backward step is felt, then fix and re-walk.
Extend: ask children to invent their own one-block bug for a partner to find and fix.
Movement option: a child acts as Bit and walks the buggy program, freezing on box 2; the class calls out the fix.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child writes box 2 for the buggy run, circles the middle ⬅ block, draws ➡ to fix it, and runs the fixed program to land Bit on box 4, the star.
